category: Layer menu II - advanced blending, matting, smart object links, shapes, video layers and quick mask
description: Layer menu commands and Layers-panel behaviours that the 'Layers, masks, smart objects and layer styles' category does not cover: Knockout and Global Light in Blending Options, the Matting submenu, the Smart Object link/relink/export commands, shape combination, video layers, background conversion, layer-style-to-layer conversion and Quick Mask editing.

tools.name: Knockout (Advanced Blending)
tools.description: A Blending Options setting that makes a layer punch a hole through the layers beneath it to reveal a deeper layer: Shallow knocks out to the bottom of the layer's group (or the first non-Pass Through group), Deep knocks out all the way to the Background. The layer's own Fill opacity sets how much of the knockout shows, so a shape at 0 % Fill with Deep knockout becomes a clean window through everything above the Background.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Blending Options... > Advanced Blending > Knockout: None / Shallow / Deep

parameters.name: Knockout
parameters.description: None (default), Shallow, Deep.

parameters.name: Fill Opacity
parameters.description: Lower it (often to 0 %) to let the knocked-out content show through the layer's pixels.

parameters.name: Blend Interior Effects as Group / Blend Clipped Layers as Group
parameters.description: Whether inner effects and clipped layers participate in the knockout.

tools.example:
1. Put a text layer inside a group above several image layers, with a Background at the bottom.
2. Double-click the text layer, set Knockout: Deep, Fill Opacity 0 %.
3. The text now shows the Background through all the image layers.
tools.notes: A group set to Normal (not Pass Through) stops a Shallow knockout at its boundary. Knockout is stored in the PSD and honoured by Export As.

tools.name: Global Light
tools.description: A single document-wide light angle and altitude shared by every layer effect that has 'Use Global Light' ticked (Drop Shadow, Inner Shadow, Bevel & Emboss). Changing it once re-lights all styles consistently, which is essential for UI mock-ups and multi-element compositions.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Global Light...   (Angle, Altitude)

parameters.name: Angle
parameters.description: -180 to 180 degrees; direction the light comes from.

parameters.name: Altitude
parameters.description: 0-90 degrees; used by Bevel & Emboss only.

parameters.name: Use Global Light (per effect)
parameters.description: Checkbox inside each effect; untick to give one effect its own angle.

tools.example: Layer > Layer Style > Global Light: Angle 135, Altitude 30 - all drop shadows in the document now fall to the bottom right.
tools.notes: Dragging the angle dial inside any effect dialog with Use Global Light on changes the global value for the whole document. The value is saved in the PSD.

tools.name: Defringe
tools.description: Replaces the colour of edge pixels of a cut-out layer with the colour of nearby interior pixels over a chosen width, removing the halo left when a selection includes a sliver of the old background. Works on transparency edges only, so the layer must already be cut out.
tools.usage: Layer > Matting > Defringe...  (Width in px)

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: 1-200 px; 1-2 px is typical, larger values smear.

tools.example: After Select Subject + Layer Via Copy, choose Layer > Matting > Defringe, Width 1, to kill the light fringe around hair.
tools.notes: Destructive; keep a copy. Select and Mask > Decontaminate Colors is the modern alternative and works on masks.

tools.name: Remove Black Matte and Remove White Matte
tools.description: Remove the dark or light fringe left when an anti-aliased element was matted against black or white (typical of renders and cut-outs saved without straight alpha). Photoshop un-premultiplies the edge pixels assuming the given matte colour, restoring clean semi-transparent edges.
tools.usage: Layer > Matting > Remove Black Matte  /  Remove White Matte
tools.example: Place a PNG logo rendered against black that shows a dark halo on a light background, then Layer > Matting > Remove Black Matte.
tools.notes: Only affects pixels with partial transparency. For arbitrary matte colours use Defringe or Decontaminate Colors.

tools.name: Color Decontaminate
tools.description: Runs the Select and Mask 'Decontaminate Colors' algorithm on a layer that already has transparency, replacing colour fringes with colour sampled from fully opaque neighbouring pixels. It is the batch-friendly, menu-based version of the Select and Mask output option.
tools.usage: Layer > Matting > Color Decontaminate
tools.example: On a layer masked with Select Subject, apply the mask (Layer > Layer Mask > Apply) and then Layer > Matting > Color Decontaminate.
tools.notes: Requires pixel transparency, not a mask; apply the mask first. Introduced in CS5.

tools.name: Combine Shapes
tools.description: Boolean operations for the paths on a shape layer or for several selected shape layers: Unite Shapes, Subtract Front Shape, Unite Shapes at Overlap (intersect) and Subtract Shapes at Overlap (exclude). The same operations appear as Path Operations in the options bar of the Pen and shape tools and in the Properties panel.
tools.usage: Layer > Combine Shapes > Unite Shapes / Subtract Front Shape / Unite Shapes at Overlap / Subtract Shapes at Overlap

parameters.name: Unite Shapes
parameters.description: Adds all shapes into one filled area.

parameters.name: Subtract Front Shape
parameters.description: Cuts the top-most shape out of the ones below.

parameters.name: Unite Shapes at Overlap
parameters.description: Keeps only the intersection.

parameters.name: Subtract Shapes at Overlap
parameters.description: Keeps everything except the intersection (exclusive OR).

tools.example: Draw a rectangle shape, then a circle shape layer above it; select both and choose Layer > Combine Shapes > Subtract Front Shape to punch the circle out of the rectangle.
tools.notes: Combining layers merges them into one shape layer with the top layer's fill and stroke. Use Path Selection tool > Merge Shape Components to bake the result into a single path.

tools.name: Video Layers
tools.description: Commands for frame-based video editing on the Timeline: create a video layer from a movie file or a blank one, insert/duplicate/delete frames, replace or reinterpret footage (frame rate, alpha, colour), and restore altered frames. Video layers accept the same filters, adjustments and layer styles as pixel layers and can be painted frame by frame (rotoscoping).
tools.usage: Layer > Video Layers > New Video Layer from File... / New Blank Video Layer / Insert Blank Frame / Duplicate Frame / Delete Frame / Replace Footage... / Interpret Footage... / Hide Altered Video / Restore Frame / Restore All Frames / Reload Frame / Rasterize

parameters.name: New Video Layer from File...
parameters.description: Imports MOV, MP4, AVI and image sequences as a video layer.

parameters.name: Interpret Footage...
parameters.description: Alpha (Ignore, Straight, Premultiplied), Frame Rate, Color Profile, De-Interlace, field order.

parameters.name: Replace Footage...
parameters.description: Swap the source file while keeping edits and effects.

parameters.name: Restore Frame / Restore All Frames
parameters.description: Discard painted alterations on a frame or all frames.

tools.example:
1. File > Import > Video Frames to Layers (for frame layers) or Layer > Video Layers > New Video Layer from File (for a timeline clip).
2. Add a Curves adjustment above it; it applies to every frame.
3. File > Export > Render Video to write H.264.
tools.notes: Requires Window > Timeline in Video Timeline mode. Painting on a video layer alters only the current frame. Video features are not available in the trial-mode 'photography' feature set on some subscriptions.

tools.name: Export Contents (Smart Object)
tools.description: Writes the source of an embedded Smart Object back to disk in its original format (PSB for pasted/converted layers, the original raw/JPEG/AI file for placed content). Use it to recover the full-resolution original or to hand a placed raw file to another application.
tools.usage: Layer > Smart Objects > Export Contents...

parameters.name: Destination
parameters.description: File dialog; the name defaults to the smart object name with the source extension.

tools.example: Select a placed .cr3 Smart Object and choose Layer > Smart Objects > Export Contents to get the untouched raw file back.
tools.notes: Linked smart objects export their current linked file. Content converted from layers exports as .psb.

tools.name: Reset Transform (Smart Object)
tools.description: Removes every scale, rotation, skew, warp and perspective transformation applied to a Smart Object, returning it to its native size and orientation without touching the contents. Also clears Puppet Warp and Perspective Warp data applied as smart transforms.
tools.usage: Layer > Smart Objects > Reset Transform
tools.example: After several Free Transform passes on a placed logo, choose Layer > Smart Objects > Reset Transform to get the pixel-exact original size back.
tools.notes: Available since CC 2015.5. The Properties panel also shows a Reset button for placed objects.

tools.name: Convert to Linked and Convert to Embedded (Smart Object)
tools.description: Switch a Smart Object between the two storage models: Convert to Linked saves the embedded contents to an external file and links to it (small PSD, shared source across documents), while Convert to Embedded copies the linked file into the PSD so it travels with the document. Linked objects show a chain icon and update when the file changes.
tools.usage: Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Linked... / Convert to Embedded

parameters.name: Convert to Linked...
parameters.description: Prompts for a location and file name for the extracted contents (.psb or original format).

parameters.name: Convert to Embedded
parameters.description: Embeds the linked file; no dialog.

tools.example: Select an embedded logo Smart Object, Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Linked..., save as logo.psb; place the same file in other documents so one edit updates all.
tools.notes: File > Package collects all linked files with the PSD for hand-off. Missing links show a red question-mark badge.

tools.name: Relink to File, Relink to Library Graphic and Update Modified Content
tools.description: Maintenance commands for linked Smart Objects: Relink to File points a broken or replaced link at a new file, Relink to Library Graphic connects it to a Creative Cloud Library asset, Update Modified Content refreshes the selected layer from its changed source and Update All Modified Content refreshes every out-of-date link in the document.
tools.usage: Layer > Smart Objects > Relink to File... / Relink to Library Graphic... / Update Modified Content / Update All Modified Content
tools.example: A yellow warning badge appears on a linked layer after editing its source in Illustrator: choose Layer > Smart Objects > Update Modified Content.
tools.notes: Preferences > File Handling has options controlling when modified links are checked. Linked files are looked up by absolute path first, then next to the PSD.

tools.name: Convert to Layers (Smart Object)
tools.description: Unpacks an embedded Smart Object back into its original layers (with masks, styles and groups) in the current document, placed inside a group named after the object. Use it when you need to edit the individual layers in context instead of in a separate window, or to remove the Smart Object wrapper without rasterising.
tools.usage: Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Layers   (also the Properties panel > Convert to Layers)
tools.example: Select a Smart Object that was made from a group of text and shape layers, choose Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Layers, and edit the text directly.
tools.notes: Introduced in Photoshop 22.0 (October 2020). Transformations and Smart Filters applied to the Smart Object are lost (a warning appears); linked objects must be embedded first.

tools.name: Isolate Layers
tools.description: Temporarily filters the Layers panel and the canvas to show only the selected layers (or the layer under the cursor when using the Move tool's Auto-Select with Ctrl+Shift+click), hiding everything else without changing visibility flags. Useful for editing one element in a crowded document and for the Path Selection tool's Isolate option on shape layers.
tools.usage: Select > Isolate Layers   (or right-click on canvas with the Move tool > Isolate Layers; the Layers panel filter switches to 'Selected')
tools.example: Ctrl-click three layers, choose Select > Isolate Layers, retouch them, then click the red toggle in the Layers panel filter bar to leave isolation.
tools.notes: Isolation is a Layers panel filter (Kind: Selected) - the eye icons are not changed, so exports are unaffected.

tools.name: Background from Layer and Layer from Background
tools.description: Converts between the locked, opaque Background layer and a normal layer. Layer from Background (or double-click the Background) unlocks it so it can be moved, masked, reordered and made transparent; Background from Layer flattens the selected layer's transparency against the background colour and locks it at the bottom, which some formats (e.g. certain JPEG/EPS workflows) and File > Automate operations expect.
tools.usage: Layer > New > Layer from Background...  /  Layer > New > Background from Layer

parameters.name: Name / Color / Mode / Opacity
parameters.description: Options offered when converting from Background to a layer.

tools.notes: Clicking the lock icon on the Background layer (CC 2017+) is the fastest way to unlock it. A document can have only one Background layer.

tools.name: Layer Style > Create Layer
tools.description: Converts each layer effect on the selected layer (Drop Shadow, Stroke, Gradient Overlay...) into its own ordinary pixel layer, clipped or positioned as the effect was. Use it to edit an effect with brushes and filters, to warp a drop shadow independently, or to export effects separately.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Create Layer  (also Layers panel: right-click the fx badge > Create Layers)
tools.example: Add a Drop Shadow, then Layer > Layer Style > Create Layer; the new 'Drop Shadow' layer can be Free Transformed to lie on the ground plane.
tools.notes: Some effects (e.g. those with Global Light or contour settings) are approximated; a warning lists what could not be reproduced exactly. The result is no longer live.

tools.name: Layer Style > Hide All Effects and Clear Layer Style
tools.description: Hide All Effects toggles the visibility of every effect on the selected layer without removing them (same as clicking the eye next to 'Effects'), and Clear Layer Style removes all effects permanently. Both are also on the Layers panel context menu and are useful in scripts that need a clean export of a layer.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Style > Hide All Effects / Show All Effects / Clear Layer Style
tools.notes: Hidden effects still count toward the layer's bounds in some exports; clear them if pixel-exact bounds matter.

tools.name: Layer Mask > From Transparency
tools.description: Creates a layer mask from the layer's own alpha channel and then makes the pixels fully opaque, moving transparency out of the pixels into an editable mask. Useful before filters that need pixels under transparent areas, and to soften or refine a hard cut-out edge non-destructively.
tools.usage: Layer > Layer Mask > From Transparency
tools.example: On a cut-out PNG layer, choose Layer > Layer Mask > From Transparency, then paint on the mask to refine the edge.
tools.notes: Introduced in CC 2014. The layer's pixels outside the former shape become whatever Photoshop extends (often black) - normally hidden by the mask.

tools.name: Layer > New > Artboard, Artboard from Group and Artboard from Layers
tools.description: Create artboards without the Artboard tool: New Artboard opens a size/preset dialog, Artboard from Group converts a selected group (keeping its contents) and Artboard from Layers wraps the selected layers in a new artboard sized to their bounds. Artboards act as independent canvases inside one document, ideal for multi-screen UI design and multiple ad sizes.
tools.usage: Layer > New > Artboard... / Artboard from Group... / Artboard from Layers...

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Artboard name (used as the file name by Export As / Artboards to Files).

parameters.name: Size / Width / Height
parameters.description: Preset (iPhone, Web, Print...) or custom dimensions in the current ruler unit.

parameters.name: Background Color (Properties panel)
parameters.description: White, Black, Transparent or Other per artboard.

tools.example: Select the layers of a banner, choose Layer > New > Artboard from Layers..., name it '300x250', then File > Export > Artboards to Files.
tools.notes: Artboards cannot be nested. Moving a layer outside all artboards makes it a document-level layer.

tools.name: Edit in Quick Mask Mode
tools.description: Temporarily turns the current selection into a red-tinted overlay that you can paint with any brush, gradient or filter, then converts it back into a selection when you exit. It is the fastest way to feather, soften or hand-paint a selection with full brush control, and the overlay colour, opacity and 'Masked/Selected Areas' meaning are set by double-clicking the toolbar button.
tools.usage: Select > Edit in Quick Mask Mode   (Q toggles; double-click the Quick Mask button for options)

parameters.name: Color Indicates
parameters.description: Masked Areas (default: red = unselected) or Selected Areas.

parameters.name: Color / Opacity
parameters.description: Overlay colour and its opacity (default red, 50 %).

tools.example:
1. Press Q, paint with a black soft brush to protect areas (red), white to select.
2. Filter > Blur > Gaussian Blur 4 px to feather the mask.
3. Press Q again - the marching ants reflect the painted mask.
tools.notes: Scripting: `app.activeDocument.quickMaskMode = true/false`. Quick Mask appears as a temporary 'Quick Mask' channel in the Channels panel.

tools.name: Layer > Rename Layer and layer naming conventions
tools.description: Rename Layer opens the in-place name editor (double-click the name does the same); Tab moves to the next layer's name while editing, which makes bulk renaming quick. Layer names drive Generate Image Assets (e.g. 'logo.png, 200% logo@2x.png'), Export As file names, Data Set variables and any script that looks up layers by name.
tools.usage: Layer > Rename Layer...   (double-click name; Tab / Shift+Tab to move between layers while renaming)
tools.example:
var lyrs = app.activeDocument.artLayers;
for (var i = 0; i < lyrs.length; i++) lyrs[i].name = "img_" + (i + 1);
tools.notes: Names need not be unique; scripts that use `layers.getByName()` return the first match. Photoshop 27.6 adds smarter automatic names for new layers.

tools.name: Layer > Lock All Layers in Group and Lock Layers dialog
tools.description: Applies lock flags (Transparency, Image, Position, Artboard nesting, All) to every layer in the selected group or selection at once through a dialog, instead of clicking the lock icons per layer. Useful before Auto-Align or when handing files to collaborators.
tools.usage: Layer > Lock Layers... (selected layers)  /  Layer > Lock All Layers in Group...

parameters.name: Transparent Pixels
parameters.description: Prevents painting on transparent areas.

parameters.name: Image Pixels
parameters.description: Prevents pixel edits.

parameters.name: Position
parameters.description: Prevents moving/transforming.

parameters.name: Prevent auto-nesting into and out of Artboards
parameters.description: Keeps the layer from changing artboard when moved.

parameters.name: All
parameters.description: All of the above.

tools.example: Select the 'guides' group and choose Layer > Lock All Layers in Group..., tick All.
tools.notes: ExtendScript: `layer.allLocked`, `pixelsLocked`, `positionLocked`, `transparentPixelsLocked`.
